findings.breaking_input: A registry-approved host's DNS is set up with a very short TTL: the record `refusePrivate`'s `dns.lookup(host,{all:true})` sees resolves to a public address (passes the private-address check), then the record is changed to 127.0.0.1 (or 169.254.169.254 for a cloud metadata endpoint) before the immediately-following `fetch(target,...)` call performs its own, independent DNS resolution and connects to the now-rebound private address.
findings.why: `refusePrivate(hostname)` and `fetch(target,...)` each resolve the hostname separately with no pinning between the two lookups. This is a classic TOCTOU/DNS-rebinding SSRF: the exact value that was checked (an IP from `dns.lookup`) is never the value actually connected to (whatever `fetch`'s own resolver returns moments later). The same `realTransport.get()` is reused for the robots.txt fetch, the screen fetch, and `checkBrowse`'s page probe, so every network boundary this file guards is bypassable the same way.
findings.fix: After `refusePrivate` validates the resolved address(es), connect to that exact validated IP (e.g. supply a custom `dispatcher`/`Agent` with a fixed `lookup`/`connect` that reuses the already-checked address while still sending the original Host/SNI), and repeat the check-and-pin on every redirect hop rather than doing a plain `fetch(target)` after a separate check.
findings.twin_of: The licence was checked on one input and the fetch made on another -> every permission check binds to the exact value that is then used.

findings.breaking_input: Any future change to `preflight()`/`decide()` that returns a verdict string outside {ALLOW, DISALLOW, UNREADABLE} (e.g. a new content-signal or timeout verdict) reaches `design-refpack.mjs`'s `check()`: `fail(EXIT[d.verdict], ...)` becomes `fail(undefined, msg)`, and `process.exit(undefined)` behaves like `process.exit()` -- exit code 0.
findings.why: `checkBrowse()` explicitly guards the identical lookup with `Object.hasOwn(EXIT, d.verdict) ? EXIT[d.verdict] : EXIT.UNREADABLE`, but the sibling lookup in the main pack-building flow's `check()` does the raw `EXIT[d.verdict]` with no such guard. A refusal that falls through this gap prints an error line to stderr but exits 0 -- a refusal that any caller checking `$?` (curator script, CI, a chained `&&`) reads as success.
findings.fix: Apply the same `Object.hasOwn(EXIT, d.verdict) ? EXIT[d.verdict] : EXIT.UNREADABLE` guard in `check()` that `checkBrowse()` already uses.
findings.twin_of: An unknown verdict looked up in a code table gave undefined, and process.exit(undefined) is 0 -> only the exact success verdict exits 0; every other lookup miss is a refusal.

findings.where: design-refpack.mjs main() sources.md row write (appendFileSync after the linkSync header creation)
findings.breaking_input: Run two `design-refpack.mjs --brief lexos ...` invocations concurrently for the same brief once `sources.md` already exists (so both skip the atomic header-creation branch and go straight to `appendFileSync(sourcesMd, row)`), e.g. a curator adding two screens back-to-back on Windows/NTFS.
findings.why: Only the header creation is made atomic (private temp file + `linkSync`). Each row append after that relies on POSIX's O_APPEND-is-atomic guarantee, but on Windows, libuv's append emulation does a separate seek-to-end-of-file followed by a write rather than one atomic append syscall, so two concurrent writers can land at the same offset and interleave or clobber each other's row -- exactly the class of Windows-only concurrent-write corruption this project has hit before with git objects.
findings.fix: Serialize row writes the same way the header is protected (write to a private temp file then atomically append via a lock file or a single-writer queue), instead of relying on bare `appendFileSync` being atomic across processes on every OS.

findings.where: design-refpack.mjs field() (control-character stripping used by every log/markdown write)
findings.breaking_input: A fetched host returns `Content-Type: image/png\u2028FAKE\tENTRY` (or a robots.txt `Disallow:` line containing U+2028), which flows through `record()`/`field()` into `availability.log`/`attempts.log`/`curator-browse.log`.
findings.why: `field()` only strips `\u0000-\u001f` and `\u007f`; it does not strip Unicode line/paragraph separators (U+2028, U+2029) or NEL (U+0085). Any tool or viewer that treats those as line breaks reads the injected text as an extra, fabricated log entry, since the values logged here (content-type, robots.txt rule text, redirect targets) are fully remote-controlled.
findings.fix: Widen `field()`'s stripped set to also remove U+2028, U+2029, U+0085 (and any other line-breaking Unicode class), not just the ASCII C0/DEL range.
findings.twin_of: Remote text reached a tab-separated log verbatim -> strip control characters from every logged field.
